questions.q: What problem does a slowly changing dimension (SCD) address?
options: How to speed up slow-running queries
What happens to the old value of a dimension attribute when it changes — like a customer's city or a product's category
How to convert a dimension table into a fact table
How fast a fact table grows over time
questions.explain: SCDs are specifically about handling changes to dimension attributes over time, not fact data.

questions.q: What happens in a Type 1 SCD change?
options: A new row is inserted with a new surrogate key
The value is simply overwritten in place — no history of the old value is preserved
An extra column is added to hold the previous value
The entire dimension table is dropped and recreated
questions.explain: Type 1 is the simplest approach: update in place, and the old value is gone.

questions.q: What happens in a Type 2 SCD change?
options: Nothing changes until the next full reload of the warehouse
The old value is simply overwritten with no trace
A new row is inserted with a new surrogate key, and the old row is marked with an end date — preserving full history
The dimension table is converted into a fact table
questions.explain: Type 2 keeps every historical version as its own row, so past fact rows still point at the version that was true at the time.

questions.q: How does AdventureWorksDW2014's DimProduct implement Type 2 tracking?
options: With real StartDate, EndDate, and Status columns — a non-NULL EndDate marks a retired version superseded by a new ProductKey
It doesn't implement any SCD tracking at all
By storing every historical version in a separate database
By using a CHECK constraint to block any updates
questions.explain: These are genuine columns in the real table, used exactly as described for Type 2 versioning.

questions.q: Why is SCD Type 2 connected to Lesson 108's 'time-variant' property?
options: Type 2 removes the need for a warehouse to be time-variant at all
It's the actual mechanism that delivers time-variance for dimension attributes, letting historical fact rows show what was true at the time, not just current values
Time-variance only applies to OLTP systems, never data warehouses
It has no real connection — time-variance only applies to fact tables
questions.explain: Without Type 2 (or similar) tracking, a dimension update would retroactively change how historical facts are reported, breaking time-variance.
